topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides introductory framing and outlines the intended learning outcomes for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional modalities: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities of cancer therapy that target tumors through physical resection, radiation-induced DNA damage, and non-selective cytotoxic mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively target cancer cells by taking advantage of their specific biological defects in signaling, cell cycle checkpoint regulation, and DNA repair.

topics.label: Targeting oncogene addiction and hyperactivated kinases
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on the therapeutic inhibition of driver oncogenic kinases and the molecular mechanisms governing drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design and application of antibody-based therapeutics to directly neutralize surface receptors or deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and cellular immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles of tumor immune recognition and the clinical application of immunotherapies that mobilize T cells against cancer.

topics.label: Systemic challenges, population trends, and future directions in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broader challenges in cancer treatment, including therapeutic resistance, epidemiological trends, and evolving ethical paradigms in patient management.
